Minutes: 
On September 8, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to 
review the July Revenue and Expenditure Report and financial items before the City Council. 
The report covered the first month of Fiscal Year 2027 and included a preliminary $5 million net 
school spending shortfall. The City also made its annual $116.5 million pension payment, the 
primary reason expenditures temporarily outpaced revenues. 
The committee reviewed several grants and funding items, including $325,000 for veterinary 
services at Thomas J. O'Connor Animal Control, approximately $490,000 for employment and 
training opportunities for low-income seniors, $765,000 in gaming mitigation funding for public 
health, public safety, and downtown economic development, and approximately $827,000 in 
housing assistance for people with HIV/AIDS.   
The committee also reviewed a donation supporting Bass Pond restoration, $1.176 million in 
additional state funding for the City's street paving program, prior-year bills, cable access 
funding, and a three-year agreement with the Springfield Business Improvement District that 
includes a $150,000 annual City contribution.   
Meeting adjourned: approximately 4:33 p.m.
